headline: Diaspora, Data, and *Dissent*
intro: This week's picks trace threads of belonging and belief — from Belarusian exiles and Venice's Caribbean reckonings to the quiet politics of doom metal and Chandigarh's unruly utopia. Elsewhere, data brokers get exposed, marble gets faked, and fashion looks homeward for inspiration.

entries.title: Alma Thomas Opens Up Our Crowns
entries.author: Alexis Pauline Gumbs
entries.summary: The cornrows of Thomas’s paintings, often inspired by her own garden, evoke the infinitely diverse ears of native corn and the sisterhood of braiders across the diaspora.

entries.title: AQUÍ NO HA PASADO NADA: VENECIA, EL CARIBE Y EL TRAUMA INTERGENERACIONAL
entries.author: Anayra Santory Jorge
entries.summary: En este ensayo, Anayra Santory Jorge examina "In Minor Keys", la exposición curada por Koyo Kouoh —primera mujer africana en dirigir la Bienal de Venecia— desde su propia posición como habitante de un archipiélago caribeño colonizado. La autora contrasta el despoblamiento y la crisis climática de Venecia con las dinámicas extractivas del turismo y el colonialismo en Puerto Rico, y usa esa tensión…

entries.author: Matthew Jones

entries.author: Derek Kravitz for Consumer Reports, Colin Lecher, and with illustrations by Catherine Twomey
entries.summary: Data brokers collect thousands of details about your finances, health and habits. See what’s in your profile, who buys it and how companies use it.

entries.title: A country between being and nothing
entries.author: Simon Garnett
entries.summary: In search of traces of the Belarusian diaspora in the West after 1945, the poet Volha Hapeyeva considers how language and literature provide a sense of belonging away from home, helping to conserve an identity that is both Belarusian and European.

entries.title: Songs You Can See: How Latin American Artists Build a Visual World Around Their Music
entries.author: Sounds and Colours
entries.summary: Think of a song you love from somewhere in Latin America. There is a good chance you can also picture something: a colour, a room, a street, a dancer, a face. Music tends to arrive with images attached. Sometimes they come from a video. Sometimes from an album sleeve, a poster taped to a wall,... Read Article
